reason: The hypothesis relies on Hf increasing lattice distortion and promoting edge dislocation dominance, but the cited evidence does not directly support this mechanism for TiVNbTa. E1 and E2 discuss strength retention in NbTaTiV and Mo-containing HEAs, mentioning edge dislocations only for MoNbTaW/VW, not for Hf-modified alloys. E3 shows Hf increases theoretical strength in MoNbTaW but does not address dislocation character or TiVNbTa. The key mechanistic premise linking Hf to edge dislocation control is unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Hf addition increases lattice distortion and adjusts elastic constants in BCC HEAs
Edge dislocation-controlled deformation yields better high-temperature strength retention than screw-dominated slip
TiVNbTa baseline has a single-phase BCC structure with ~330 MPa yield strength at 1273 K
MoNbTaW and MoNbTaVW retain high-temperature strength via edge dislocation mechanisms
Hf-containing BCC HEAs can show enhanced theoretical strength and high melting points
